name: Teetly
about:
Hi! I go by Teetly, and I am a first-year PhD student in Biomedical Informatics at Vanderbilt University. Prior to my PhD, I worked in high-performance computing, particularly improving LLM performance in generating low-resource languages, and in computational biology research focused on protein structure representation learning.

My research interests include:

1. Multimodal Representation Learning: How can we integrate imaging data with clinical notes to develop a more comprehensive patient-level understanding?

2. Medical Imaging: I am currently working on causal synthesis models for dermatology.

news.text: Gave an oral presentation on "Evaluating LLM Generated Task Codes" at the 31st HIPS Workshop, held at IPDPS.
Received the Schultz Foundation Travel Award and Lazarus Center Professional Development Fund.
Gave an oral presentation titled "Fine Tuning Convergence Experiments with Large Language Models Trained on High Performance Computing Code" at Celebrating Collaborations at Smith College.
Presented the poster "Encoding Essential Features in Protein Structure for Task Generalization" at RosettaCon.
